summary: Test-only guards against two silent regressions. The CAD body loss search skips removed pieces whose keys stay in a group, since none of their keys can be lost, and a domain test now makes that skip observable through the search's own step count: in two nested splits of 2,000 pieces that the kernel may order any way, reading the keys of one removed piece passes MAX_CAD_BODY_ORDER_WORK and leaves the body untracked, while the same piece kept in a carried group, or in the group a solid keeping no face makes, is never read and the body stays tracked. Removing the skip fails the test. Three section cap tests checked caps as soon as a build started, under the view's 6 ms time slice, so a slow runner could leave a cap for a later slice and fail them; they now build caps in one go, as the other cap tests do.
warning: No breaking change for installed posts, machine packages, saved revisions, CAD files or controller output. Only tests change: no application code, schema, agent tool, diagnostic or stored data.

checklist.verification: src/domain/cad/__tests__/cadBodies.test.ts adds "never reads the keys of a removed piece that stays in a group, which can take more steps than the work bound" (59 tests). Its first case removes one inner piece of two nested 2,000-piece splits in any kernel order, outside any group: none of its keys is lost, since each names a sibling left in another order, but reading them takes about 2 × 2,000² steps, so the body is untracked and overflowed. That case pins the count. The steps are the search's own, so no clock decides the outcome, and should a cheaper search ever bring it under the bound, the case fails and the test needs a larger body instead of silently guarding nothing. The same piece in a group that a continued piece descends from, and in the group that a solid keeping no face makes with every piece continued alone, leaves the body tracked with no lost key. Removing the skip, the stays filter in cadBodyParts, fails each of the two cases alone; no other test in the file fails. The search's candidates are pieces no solid continues and members of groups nothing descends from, and neither is a piece afterwards: a group is the only way one stays. The per-solid bound on lost keys, the check inside the search that stops once one solid's list passes MAX_CAD_BODY_LIST, gets no count test. The search counts reading steps, which that bound does not change, and the result is the same without it, since the bound on the feature's total then refuses the list. What it bounds is the list, which nested splits multiply: without it, a chain of n two-piece splits in any order whose deepest pair goes builds 2^n keys for one solid before the total refuses them. Measured at a depth of 21, that is a list of 2,097,152 keys, built in 1.6 s with 306 MB more heap, against about 1 ms at every depth with the bound, so the bound holds memory as well as time, beyond the longer list the 0.0.801 record describes. A test could see it only by patching a builtin such as Array.prototype.push, which would stop seeing it, silently, if the search built its list another way, or by a depth whose unbounded list exhausts memory, which crashes the test worker instead of failing a check. Section caps: in src/features/cad/view/cadSectionCaps.test.ts, "caps every cut body where it lies, far from the origin too, and none it does not cut or that is open" and "builds caps once for each plane and upload, keeps them while hidden, and draws nothing when no body is cut" called createCadSectionCaps() with the default 6 ms slice and checked at once. They now pass { sliceMs: Infinity }, as the neighbouring tests do. With { sliceMs: 0 } there instead, standing in for a slow runner, the first fails as F0's unit shard 1 once did, showing only the near cap, and the second finds the cap it hid rebuilt. A search of the source for time-sliced work found two: CAD_SECTION_CAP_SLICE_MS in cadSectionCaps.ts, and the 8 ms read turns of exactTextStream.ts, whose tests await the whole stream, so a slice can't race a check. src/features/cad/CadViewportSection.test.tsx builds real caps through CadViewport under the default slice: with the slice set to 0 its caps test fails where caps hidden mid-build are dropped and rebuilt. It now builds them in one go through a module mock that passes { sliceMs: Infinity }. CadPlaneSelectionSection.test.tsx and CadWorkbench.test.tsx mock the viewport, so they build no caps, and cadSectionCapsImport.test.ts already passes { sliceMs: Infinity }. The collision scan and the package input reader yield by count, not time. Checks at 416fbc7d, the test commit, with this version and record: the focused suites pass (130 files and 1,518 tests: src/domain/cad, src/features/cad/view, src/features/cad/CadViewportSection.test.tsx and src/features/cad/kernel/cadKernelBodies.test.ts, including cadBodies.test.ts with 59 tests in 3.9 s, about 0.4 s of it the new test); npm run build passes, including the app type check, the documentation build and check and the corresponding-source checks; npm run lint has zero findings over 636 source files; npm run ui:check passes; check-release passes on its own, while against origin/main it reports this record's previousVersion 0.0.803 where main is at 0.0.801, until the number is set at merge; the branch and title pass the pull request naming check; git diff --check is clean. The full Vitest run and the browser journeys run in continuous integration.
